title: Next Greater Node In Linked List
summary: Given a linked list with n nodes, for each node, determine the value of the first subsequent node that has a strictly larger value.
statement: Given a linked list with n nodes, for each node, determine the value of the first subsequent node that has a strictly larger value. Return an array where each element corresponds to the value of the next greater node for the respective node in the list, or 0 if no such node exists.
constraints: Return one value per node; use zero when no later strictly larger value exists.
The input list is not modified.
reference_solution:
def next_greater_linked_values(head):
 values=[]
 while head:values.append(head.val);head=head.next
 answer=[0]*len(values);stack=[]
 for i,value in enumerate(values):
  while stack and values[stack[-1]]<value:answer[stack.pop()]=value
  stack.append(i)
 return answer

hints: Convert the linked list to values so output positions are addressable.
Keep indices whose next greater value is unresolved in a decreasing stack.
When a new value is larger, pop and fill those answers; unresolved indices remain zero.
The first value that pops an index is exactly its earliest strictly larger successor.
